difficulty.notes: String-array obfuscated build (988a36fc) — NOTE this is a DIFFERENT build than 1.json's label (ccd23f99): the property keys are decoded via Qe([char-codes]) and the md5 routine is a reassigned local (v=...), so it cannot be isolated as its own function. The anchor is therefore the login param-builder regenerator that binds hash: md5(password).toUpperCase(). The companion case9 (username encryptedParams) is NOT buildable from this capture: its encryptor is a dynamically-keyed method d[Qe([...])] with no static function span.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The login param-builder regenerator that computes md5(password).toUpperCase() and binds it to the hash field; not the Qe string decoder.

behavior_category.subtype: uppercase MD5 of password as request hash field
behavior_category.recompute_check: md5('13819912565').toUpperCase() === '9E2BFBE3D7050EDF876679FE5CE6E5AA' (verifies the semantics; the md5 routine itself is not isolable in this obfuscated build)

near_categories.why_not: A single credential field (password) is hashed, not the whole request body.
The value is MD5 of user input, not a device/browser digest.

evidence: String-array obfuscation hides field names (Qe) and the md5 routine; no source map; the anchor is an anonymous regenerator.
The same login flow also encrypts the username (encryptedParams) — a sibling field — in an adjacent regenerator.
The hash is bound inside a regenerator-compiled async login params builder reached through obfuscated indirection.

provenance.label_points_to: an older build (ccd23f99); the captured build is 2395.988a36fc.chunk.js. Located by content search for the hash binding.
